explanation: Inheriting constructors allow a derived class to automatically inherit constructors from its base class, enabling object creation with the same parameter sets without explicitly redefining them. This feature simplifies code maintenance and enhances code reuse, especially in complex class hierarchies, by reducing boilerplate and ensuring consistent construction semantics across related classes. Introduced in C++11, inheriting constructors are particularly useful in modern C++ for leveraging existing base class constructors seamlessly within derived classes.
code_example: Base(int x) { std::cout << "Constructor with int: " << x << std::endl; }
using Base::Base; // Inherit constructors from Base
example_explanation: This example demonstrates inheriting constructors by defining a derived class 'Derived' that uses 'using Base::Base;' to inherit all constructors from 'Base'. In 'main', creating 'd1' invokes the default constructor of 'Base', while 'd2' invokes the constructor of 'Base' that takes an int. This showcases how inheriting constructors enable derived classes to be instantiated with the same parameter sets as their base classes, promoting code reuse and reducing boilerplate in modern C++.
